title.en: Compute gross profit, operating, operating profit and net profit ratios

say.en: Revenue of 20 rupees lakh sounds impressive, but what matters to owners is how much of it is left as profit, and what return their capital earns. In this lesson: Compute gross profit, operating, operating profit and net profit ratios.
Compute return on investment.
Interpret profitability.

body.en: Gross profit ratio = Gross profit ÷ Revenue from operations × 100. Operating ratio = (Cost of revenue from operations + Operating expenses) ÷ Revenue from operations × 100. Operating profit ratio = Operating profit ÷ Revenue from operations × 100 = 100 − Operating ratio. Net profit ratio = Net profit ÷ Revenue from operations × 100.
body.kn: ಒಟ್ಟು ಲಾಭ, ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಲಾಭ ಮತ್ತು ನಿವ್ವಳ ಲಾಭ ಅನುಪಾತಗಳು ಆದಾಯದ ಎಷ್ಟು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಲಾಭವಾಗಿ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಅನುಪಾತ + ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಲಾಭ ಅನುಪಾತ = 100.

problem.en: Revenue from operations ₹20,00,000; cost of revenue ₹14,00,000; operating expenses ₹2,00,000; profit after tax ₹2,80,000. Find GP ratio, operating ratio, operating profit ratio and net profit ratio.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Revenue from operations 20,00,000 rupees; cost of revenue 14,00,000 rupees; operating expenses 2,00,000 rupees; profit after tax 2,80,000 rupees. Find GP ratio, operating ratio, operating profit ratio and net profit ratio.
GP equals 6,00,000 rupees; GP ratio equals 6,00,000 divided by 20,00,000 times 100 equals 30 percent.
Operating ratio equals (14,00,000 plus 2,00,000) divided by 20,00,000 times 100 equals 80 percent.
Operating profit ratio equals 100 minus 80 equals 20 percent.
Net profit ratio equals 2,80,000 divided by 20,00,000 times 100 equals 14 percent.
So the answer is 30 percent, 80 percent, 20 percent, 14 percent.

problem.en: Profit before interest and tax ₹3,00,000; shareholders’ funds ₹10,00,000; 10% debentures ₹5,00,000. Find return on investment.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Profit before interest and tax 3,00,000 rupees; shareholders' funds 10,00,000 rupees; 10 percent debentures 5,00,000 rupees. Find return on investment.
Capital employed equals 10,00,000 plus 5,00,000 equals 15,00,000 rupees.
ROI equals 3,00,000 divided by 15,00,000 times 100 equals 20 percent.
So the answer is 20 percent.
